Extremely Unprofessional Real Estate Agent in London, Ontario

Yingen Xue is one of the most unprofessional real estate agents I have encountered in London, Ontario.

A house showing was scheduled between 5:00 PM and 6:00 PM. However, at around 4:30 PM, the agent arrived with his buyer and was walking around our private property, looking through the windows while the seller’s family was still inside the house.

As a real estate professional, he should understand basic professional etiquette and respect the seller’s privacy. If an agent arrives for a scheduled showing, the proper procedure is to contact the listing agent, confirm their arrival, and obtain access through the lockbox as instructed.

Instead, walking around the property, looking through windows, and ringing the doorbell while the family is still inside is completely inappropriate and unprofessional.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed and upset with my experience with Anni Dosanjh.

For the past two months, I repeatedly contacted her almost every week asking for updates and meaningful progress on my case. Despite my repeated requests, I saw no meaningful progress. I was repeatedly left waiting and was told that research was being done.

After two months of following up, I finally received a draft yesterday. The draft was extremely general and, from my perspective, contained essentially addresses and did not meaningfully address the specific circumstances of my case.

This matter involves my child and is extremely important and emotionally difficult for me. Having to repeatedly chase my lawyer for updates, wait for weeks without meaningful progress, and continuously worry about what was happening with my case caused me significant emotional distress and stress. I personally experienced the situation as extremely mentally and emotionally exhausting.

Now that I have asked to end the relationship and receive my funds back, I have been told that approximately $2,000 will be deducted for research. I find this particularly concerning given the lack of meaningful progress I experienced during these two months. The research I have been told about has not been explained to me in a way that demonstrates how it actually benefited or advanced my case.

I have requested a complete, itemized account showing exactly what work was performed, when it was performed, how much time was spent, and how the $2,000 charge was calculated.

I feel that two very important months were wasted while I repeatedly asked for my case to move forward. The lack of communication, lack of visible progress, and uncertainty surrounding my child’s case caused me significant stress and emotional hardship.

Based on my personal experience, I would not recommend this lawyer to anyone who expects timely communication, meaningful progress, transparency, and proactive handling of an important family matter.

This company greatly disappointed me. After putting my dog Hunter down on September 4th at Raps I paid to get his ashes back. I was told by Raps I'd be notified when his ashes came back to them. Yesterday I recieved a disturbing email from Gateway asking me if I wanted to pay $370.00 to spend one half hour with my beloved Hunter. This is what it said:

"The viewing and visitation service would include 30 minutes of visitation time with Hunter, you would then be present for their placement into the private cremation chamber, the doors closing and the process starting and Hunter would be ready to go home with you later the same day. This service has an additional fee of $370 plus tax, which would be payable at our care center on the day of the viewing. Currently we are booking into late this week, or early next week"

I didn't want to have a visual about my Hunter going into the "chamber". If this is the wording they send the owners of the pets it's a bit to graphic! I never wanted a visual of this part of my baby happening and tried to put this out of my mind until this email.

When I called them they blamed Raps and said that Raps called them to let them know I wanted this. Raps blames them. So no one is taking accountability!

So, I don't know if it's a sales email pitched at the very last moment? Why wouldn't Raps tell me another visitation of my baby boy would be possible?

I am going to talk with Raps and suggest they not use this company!
This has absolutely bothered me!

Deeks used to be extremely good. I used to deal with a specific broker and we were able to take care of my insurance needs with ease. In or around covid time they made a major switch and no longer had any of their regular brokers.
When I asked what happened to the brokers I had dealt with I was told they no longer are employed by Deeks. Deeks switched to a 'call centre' style where you can get any given person and no longer have the personal service that made them great to work with.

Because of all the changes and their raising prices I decided it was time for a change, when I informed them of my leaving Deeks they included a $200 add-on to my final bill with no description. I tried a couple times to ask what the $200 was on the bill and I received no response.

I then received another email that if I did not pay the $200 before a final date that they would send a collection agency to receive the funds. I asked again in that email what the charge was for and was not given an explanation.

I ended up paying it so that this matter would be done with, but I was really unimpressed with how Deeks handled their business and would not recommend them as they are run now.

I had PRP for the first time at Skin Vitality. I specifically told the clinic that this was my first PRP treatment, but I wasn’t given clear information about what to expect.

When I originally booked the appointment, I wasn’t told that redness could last for several days. I only found this out on the day of the procedure, after I asked the nurse and had to reschedule my appointment to Friday so that I can stay home the next day. I feel this information should have been provided beforehand so I could properly plan.

I also asked the nurse multiple times to send me the post-treatment instructions, but I never received them after I went home. I later received a text asking for feedback, and I mentioned that I was unhappy because I still hadn’t received the instructions. They finally sent them the following day.

I also developed significant bruising under my left eye. Now, almost 10 days later, I still have pain and puffiness under my left eye, which is very concerning to me. I’m worried that the injection may have caused an injury to the tissue, and unfortunately, no one from the clinic has followed up with me to ask how I’m doing.

I understand that bruising can happen after PRP, but the lack of communication, delayed aftercare instructions, and complete lack of follow-up made my first experience with Skin Vitality very disappointing. I do not consider this level of communication and patient follow-up professional, especially for a first-time patient.

Absolutely disgraceful and unacceptable experience.

On Saturday, August 29, I took a taxi from the Holiday Inn & Suites Vancouver Downtown to Canadian Crafts. The fare was approximately CAD 19.53.

I later discovered that I had been charged TWICE for exactly the same ride: once in Canadian dollars and a second time in euros, for approximately €19. The euro transaction was not only an additional charge for the same journey, but it was also significantly higher than the actual value of the fare.

In other words, I ended up paying twice for a single taxi ride, with one of the payments processed in a completely different currency and at an inflated amount.

I find this conduct extremely serious, dishonest and completely unacceptable. This is not a minor exchange-rate issue or a difference of a few cents: there are two separate charges for the same ride.

I have credit card screenshots clearly documenting both transactions, and I contacted the company requesting a refund of the amount improperly charged in euros.

What makes the situation even more absurd is that the company refused to refund me because they supposedly “do not operate in Italy.” This response makes absolutely no sense. The taxi ride took place in Vancouver, and my complaint concerns a double charge for a service provided there. The fact that I live in or have since returned to Italy has nothing whatsoever to do with the legitimacy of my refund request.

For a tourist relying on a taxi service and expecting honesty, transparency and proper customer support when something goes wrong, this experience is simply unacceptable.

I expect the company to identify the driver, properly investigate what happened and refund the money that was wrongly charged to me.

Based both on what happened during the ride and on the way my complaint has subsequently been handled, I absolutely cannot recommend this company.

one_star_reviews.text:
I went in with so much trust and optimism, and left feeling lied to and financially exploited. Please don't fill out their intake form, it asks extremely personal questions and it makes it harder to walk away once you've handed over your and your family's privacy.

This was my experience with their $5k signature package:

AI-Written Report
I was charged $980 for the psychologist to write my final report. Only after paying for and receiving the report, did I see that it was filled with boiler-plate text that didn't apply to me and AI-style errors. The report was also filled with long verbatim quotes from me, even thought I hadn't seen my psychologist take notes in our appointment. The clinic did not tell me about the AI in advance, they only told me months later when I asked why my report looked the way it did.

Actual vs Stated Psychologist Credentials:
They charged me $280/hour for the 3.0 hours I spent being assessed by their psychologist, who they repeatedly referred to as “Dr.” in their emails and texts to me (see attached photo for example). That rate seemed fair for someone with a PhD education. Unfortunately, when I looked her up through the College of Psychologists (see screenshot), her highest degree is a master’s.

Lack of Claimed "Research" Behind Methods:
The clinic website (see attached screen shot) stated that their signature package used a "well-researched" tool -  the MIGDAS. After going through the MIGDAS assessment, and it not feeling scientific, I used my experience writing systematic review articles to look for the promised research. I couldn't find any peer-reviewed articles validating the MIGDAS, only suggestions that validating research is lacking (see attached photos).

Psychometric Testing Done by a Computer:
They charged me $700.00 for two and a half hours of cognitive testing over zoom with a psychometrist (see photo of invoice). Over half of the testing was done by a computer program (CNS Vital Signs). The psychometrist asked me to follow a link and then screen share so she could read the instructions on my screen out loud to me as I worked through the series of tests. This felt odd because I could read the instructions perfectly well myself, and she had just tested my reading comprehension skills, so she knew that. I emailed CNS Vital Signs afterwards and asked them about their test, they told me: “The test is self-administered, so as long as they [the patient] can read at a 4th grade reading level, they should be able to take the test (in clinic or remotely) without assistance.” $280/hour is a lot to pay for someone to watch you complete a self-administered test.

Unexplained Scoring Fees:
They charged $1960.00 for the ‘scoring of psychological material’ but asked me to complete the questionnaires online. In my experience with questionnaires in my research work, online psychological questionnaires are normally scored automatically by the questionnaire platform. The clinic also billed me separately for the cost of the questionnaires under “materials”, so I don’t understand what this two grand was used for.

Over Billing for Time with Psychologist:
If you work with this clinic, please check that they only bill you for the psychological services they book you for. The clinic charged me for an hour and a half of feedback ($420.00), but they only booked me for 60-minutes of feedback, and I only spent 60 minutes with the psychologist for this debrief (see the photos of my invoice vs booked times).

Overall, I no longer see this organization as trustworthy. As I stated earlier, I strongly recommend you do not complete their intake questionnaire unless you are completely convinced you want to work with them. Once you complete it, it's harder to walk away. My recommendation is to seek care in the public health care system.

Avoid at all cost! The administrative process was disorganized, time-consuming, and unnecessarily frustrating. The rates are excessively expensive and completely disproportionate to the quality of service provided. Based on my experience, I would not recommend this clinic. I would give 0 starts if it was possible.

one_star_reviews.text:
I was a fairly regular customer here at one point, and the staff have always been friendly and helpful. They would recognize me when I came in, which makes this experience all the more disappointing. I purchased a package of ten pre-rolls, only to discover when I got home that it contained nine instead of ten, and one of those nine was visibly damaged and squished. Obviously, mistakes can happen during packaging. What matters is how a business responds when a customer brings a legitimate problem to its attention.I called the store immediately and was told to contact the supplier. The supplier flat out said that they would do nothing. I then returned to the store in person, only to be told that their policy was zero refunds, even though I had been sold a product that was both incomplete and damaged. I understand that businesses need policies, but a blanket “no refunds” policy should not be an excuse to avoid taking responsibility for a defective product. I wasn't asking for special treatment or trying to return something I simply didn't like. I was asking them to address a straightforward mistake that resulted in me paying for a product I did not receive in acceptable condition. What makes this particularly disappointing is that I had been a regular customer and had always had positive interactions with the staff. Unfortunately, when there was an actual problem, the business chose to pass the responsibility to the supplier rather than stand behind the product it sold.

In the end, they sold me a faulty product and then refused to take ownership of a very simple mistake. That's not how you build customer loyalty.

Do better.

one_star_reviews.text:
I have never written a review for anything in my life but the experience I had at this restaurant was so terrible that I felt compelled to publicly warn anyone considering dining here, especially if you are considering coming here for a special occasion where you don’t want to leave feeling disrespected. When my partner and I planned our trip to Victoria, this restaurant was our “must visit” because he had a good experience here years ago and wanted to have his birthday dinner here.

I want to make it clear that the waitresses were great, however, the chef we had was horrible. He was awkward, low energy, and made sarcastic and borderline disrespectful jokes. When he wheeled his tray over to the table to start cooking, I gave him a big smile only to be met with a sullen expression. I thought, OK that’s a bit unexpected but not a big deal. He proceeds to ask the table if anyone was celebrating anything, in which one of the guests points to my partner to say it was his birthday (we chose to not buy the $5 birthday song package lol). The chef paused for 5-10 seconds and then said “happy birthday” in the most unenthused way, almost like he wasn’t going to say anything in response but remembered that he was working as a teppanyaki(!!!) chef. He later cut off all the shrimp tails he was cooking for the group and placed it all on my partner’s plate and said it was his birthday gift. The tails were left on his plate the entire time we were there. This could have been a funny joke if he built some kind of positive rapport with his diners throughout the night, but this felt very disrespectful.

This whole situation would not be such an issue if the entire gimmick of this place wasn’t to have a chef cook in front of you and provide an “experience”. This chef would be more suited working in a ‘normal’ restaurant, and not one that involves chefs being hospitable and interacting with guests. The food was OK and overpriced for what you get, but the attitude of the chef is really the make-or-break here. This specific chef mentioned that he had been working here for 13 years, so I’m hoping this was just an off day for him. However, for anyone considering coming here to celebrate something special, I would not risk the possibility of being assigned this teppanyaki(!!!!!!!!!!!) chef that does not want to be there, cannot read the room, or care about creating a positive experience for his guests.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointed with the customer service at GoodLife today.

I have been here for almost two hours, and during that time I’ve repeatedly noticed staff members standing around chatting and laughing instead of taking care of basic responsibilities. I even informed them that the paper towel dispensers were empty, and instead of addressing it, they simply smiled and walked away.

I understand that staff members need to communicate with each other, but when there are 3–4 employees standing around talking while basic things like paper towels are not being refilled, it is frustrating as a paying member.

We pay membership fees expecting a clean, properly maintained facility and reasonable customer service. If members have to keep reminding staff about basic maintenance and cleanliness, then it raises the question of what we are actually paying for.

I hope management takes this feedback seriously and focuses on staff accountability, cleanliness, equipment maintenance, and providing members with the service they are paying for.

When will additional funding be allocated for preventative maintenance and timely equipment repairs?

In a busy gym, frequently used machines should not remain out of order for extended periods. Members expect reliable access to well maintained equipment, and prolonged downtime reduces membership value, satisfaction, and retention.

Preventative maintenance and prompt repairs should be treated as investments in member loyalty, recurring revenue, and long term stability.  Will management commit additional resources to keep equipment reliable, minimize downtime, and meet member demand?

Very disappointing and frustrating experience with this dealer.

The car was listed on their website last week and I called the same day. I was told the car had been “sold,” not reserved, and I saw later that listing was removed.

The car appeared on the website again over the weekend. My gf liked it so much that we drove three hours early Monday morning intending to buy it outright, without financing.

Because we had travelled so far, we decided to wait for confirmation regarding the other buyer. We eventually waited in our car and called again that afternoon. We were again told “the car has been sold.” My another call went unanswered.

Based on my experience, the communication regarding this vehicle’s availability was extremely inconsistent, and I do not feel our time and effort were respected.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’m unfortunately very disappointed with my experience at this clinic and would not recommend them based on the care I received.

I originally came here because a friend who knows the owner spoke very highly of the clinic, so I genuinely thought I would be in good hands. Unfortunately, after spending thousands of dollars here, I left feeling like my care was focused more on money than on properly looking after me as a patient.

I also don’t have dental insurance, so everything I’ve paid for has been entirely out of pocket.

One of my biggest disappointments is a crown I had done here about two years ago on one of my front teeth, which cost me well over $2,000. The crown doesn’t properly match my surrounding teeth and has a noticeably darker appearance near the gumline. Because it’s a front tooth, it’s something I see every single day and am now very unhappy with.

After switching to a new dentist, I was told there isn’t really anything that can be done to correct the appearance other than replacing the crown. They also explained that they would normally colour-match a front crown to the surrounding teeth and would not expect this type of dark appearance near the gums.

So after already spending thousands of dollars at this clinic, I’m potentially looking at spending thousands more to replace dental work that is only about two years old.

There were also other aspects of my treatment that I feel could have been handled much better and potentially saved me a significant amount of money had I received more appropriate care from the beginning.

It’s extremely frustrating, especially as someone paying entirely out of pocket, to invest this much money into dental care and then have to pay another clinic to correct or replace the work. I trusted this clinic based on the recommendation I received, but unfortunately I don’t feel that I was properly taken care of, and I really wish I had gone elsewhere from the start.

Upon receiving the package, I noticed that I didn't have the oracle decks I had won, so I sent a friendly message to the owner for an explanation (I figured it was probably an oversight). The response I received was that she didn't remember me winning and that she had never done a reading for the two oracle decks mentioned. I sent her proof that they had indeed been done during her live streams, but she replied that it had been too long. I decided to move on and drop one oracle because I wasn't sure of the exact title anymore, but I was 100,000% certain about the second one because I'd wanted it for a long time and had even mentioned it the day before and on the day itself.
The owner agreed to send it to me on the condition that I pay $22 for shipping. I explained to her that I shouldn't have to pay for an item that should have been in my original order, for which I'd already paid for shipping. A few days passed without any response from her before I realized I'd been blocked on her Facebook and TikTok accounts. I messaged her from my second TikTok account and received a reply saying she'd given enough time to this and blocked me again.

In short, I received terrible customer service from her, even though I remained polite throughout our interactions, and judging by the comments from other former clients, I think it's "her trademark"....

I am posting my first one-star review to warn others about the profoundly negative experience my family endured under the care of Sue Cook at Family TLC. My three sons and I were required to participate in court-ordered “reconciliation” therapy intended to help them reconnect with their father. This process was not only ineffective but also deeply distressing and traumatic, especially for my children, due to Ms. Cook’s approach and lack of understanding of complex family dynamics involving Narcissistic Personality Disorder.

Despite the Children’s Aid Society having deemed him emotionally abusive and imposing weekly supervised visits, Ms. Cook’s report portrayed him in an unduly positive light. Her conclusions were shockingly disconnected from the reality of his behaviour and posed a risk of granting him increased time with our children, an outcome that would have been highly damaging given his history. Throughout the sessions, Ms. Cook exhibited a clear bias and was unwilling to acknowledge our legitimate concerns, dismissing the very real harm he has caused.

Fortunately, her report did not hold weight in the final decision, as other evidence of my ex-husband’s abusive behaviour ultimately overrode her recommendations. I am deeply grateful that the other evidence was given priority, sparing my children from what could have been an extremely harmful outcome.

Sue Cook’s lack of insight into the dynamics of narcissistic abuse, particularly within a family context, makes her wholly unfit to handle cases requiring a nuanced understanding and protection for vulnerable parties. Under no circumstances would I recommend her or her services for reconciliation therapy. In cases where there is a history of emotional abuse or narcissistic traits, engaging with her poses significant risks and could do more harm than good.

For the well-being of your family, I urge you to seek help elsewhere.

Update in response to Family TLC:

Your response is simply not good enough. Referring to court ordered therapy as “challenging” completely minimizes what my children and I experienced. The recommendations made by Sue Cook had the potential to drastically alter the custody of my children and our lives. Thankfully, the court had substantial other evidence before it and her recommendations did not determine the outcome.

What is missing from your response is accountability. When a professional is entrusted with decisions and recommendations that can profoundly affect children and families, there needs to be accountability when that process causes harm. Saying that Family TLC stopped providing court mandated family legal services in December 2022 does not address what happened to my family.

In fact, based on our experience, I am extremely relieved that Sue Cook no longer provides this type of reconciliation therapy. I do not believe she demonstrated the neutrality, judgment or understanding of complex family abuse dynamics necessary for work carrying such serious consequences.

I stand firmly behind this review. I would never recommend Sue Cook to anyone, under any circumstances. My family lived through the consequences of her involvement, and no carefully worded response from Family TLC changes that experience.

one_star_reviews.text:
Unfortunately, I had a very disappointing experience with AMJ during my most recent service appointment arranged through Design Within Reach.

This was already the second visit for my Noguchi Coffee Table. The original purpose of this appointment was to replace the glass top because the previous one had a small scratch, and to address a gap between the wood base pieces after the table had previously been assembled by AMJ.

From the beginning of the appointment, I did not feel that my questions or concerns were being handled professionally or respectfully. Even something as simple as asking whether they had a measuring tape was met with, “I can measure on the phone.”

More importantly, I asked both technicians whether they had experience assembling a Noguchi Table. One told me no, while the other was unsure. Since this was already the second visit and the base needed to be reassembled correctly, that understandably concerned me. I immediately contacted my DWR Design Specialist, who spoke with them directly and sent over the official assembly instructions.

I specifically asked them to review the assembly instructions before touching the base. However, while one technician was receiving the PDF, the other had already started trying to take the table apart. I immediately asked him to stop and wait until they had reviewed the instructions. This made me extremely uncomfortable because I had already explained my concern about damaging the table, and it felt like there was very little respect for the piece or for my request to follow the proper procedure.

I had no issue with them simply saying, “We haven’t assembled this particular table before, but we’re happy to review the instructions and make sure we do it correctly.” That would have been completely reasonable. Instead, their attitude made me feel as though I was somehow questioning their professionalism simply by asking them to follow the instructions for a product they had just acknowledged they were unfamiliar with. I was also very uncomfortable with the way one of the technicians spoke to my DWR Design Specialist when I called her for assistance.

Before leaving, they told me that the wood base was “only three pieces” and that even a teenager could assemble it. I found that comment particularly dismissive and unnecessary. The fact that a piece has only a few components does not mean there is no correct way to assemble and position them. In fact, the reason they were there was partly because the base had not been properly fitted during a previous service visit.

After they took the base apart and reassembled it, the gap was still there and the issue was ultimately not resolved.

My biggest issue is not that these technicians had never assembled a Noguchi Table before. Nobody can be expected to have experience with every piece of furniture. My issue is how they responded to that lack of experience. Taking a few minutes to review the manufacturer’s instructions and treating a customer’s concerns with respect would have made this an entirely different experience.

For a company handling and assembling expensive furniture, I expected considerably more care, professionalism, and attention to detail.

The appointment with the hygienist went very well, and I have no complaints about the care I received. Unfortunately, my experience with the reception and billing was very disappointing.

Before having the X-rays taken, I asked what was included in the cleaning exam. I was told that panoramic X-rays were, so I relied on that information.

However, when it came time to pay, I was told that the X-rays cost $110 and were not included in the cleaning exam covered by the Canadian plan. I explained that I had been told the opposite and asked the hygienist to confirm this information. She confirmed that this was indeed what I had been told.

Despite this, I was told that "it doesn't change anything," since the X-rays had already been taken and I still had to pay for them. I also asked if it was possible to consult with a supervisor to find a solution or at least to have the situation reviewed, but my request was denied.

When I explained that I wasn't in a financial position to easily absorb an unexpected expense, I simply expected a little understanding, an apology, or an attempt to investigate. Instead, I was told I was exaggerating given the amount of the expense in question.

I find it regrettable that an error in information can ultimately be entirely borne by the customer.

I would personally not recommend this establishment for vegans. I'll explain in August 2026 me and my family went to pizza pizza on Boulevard Maloney in Gatineau to order a extra large pizza with dairy-free cheese. The plant-based option of course. Seeing that there's no other Pizzeria around our vicinity, we decided to go to pizza pizza in Gatineau on Maloney Boulevard.Before ordering the pizza in person at that location I had asked the cashier to make sure that it was plant-based cheese and nothing else on the pizza. She assured me that it would be 100% plant-based cheese so I trusted. Then the pizza came out after she gave me the pizza. I opened the pizza once I got in my truck to realize that she had not put plant-based cheese on it. She had put regular cheese dairy cheese . So like every good customer I went back to that location and told the same clerk that I ordered the pizza and specified that it had to be plant-based cheese only on the pizza. She said her assuring voice I guarantee you Sir This is not dairy cheese it's plant-based cheese. She did her verification in front of me with the person that had made the pizza and sure enough she had mixed dairy cheese with plant-based cheese. I kept my cool and I told the cashier I had asked for plant-based cheese and you give me dairy cheese. She assured me that she would be doing the pizza herself and would only put plant-based cheese like I had asked at that point. 30 minutes had passed since I ordered the first pizza. Then she cooked a brand new pizza for me. Once that was done another 15 minutes had passed. So that's 45 minutes total of weight. She opened the pizza box. I verified it. It was plant-based cheese. The only thing I can say for vegans going to location is be wary of the fact that they do not wear gloves so they do not respect the sanitary conditions. They don't wash their workplace so always be mindful of that. I'm not giving a good review to this location because of the sanitary conditions and the lack of professionalism and customer service. So to make this short. If you can I would strongly not recommend this location and to all my vegan family other pizza pizzas like Almer pizza pizza are much more sanitary and better establishment , awesome customer service to purchase your next pizza

one_star_reviews.text:
**Avoid this property and management company.**

Days before our move, we were told the furnished unit we had originally discussed had been rented to someone else. The only alternative offered was a more expensive unit on a lower floor, which left us with very little choice given how close we were to our move date.

Before agreeing to it, we specifically asked whether there was any significant outside noise and were told it was a non-issue. That was completely misleading. The building is affected by frequent train noise and substantial noise from the nearby shipyard. Trains, heavy machinery, and industrial activity start as early as 4:00 a.m. and continue throughout the day into the evening. The noise is persistent and can be extremely disruptive, especially when trying to sleep. Failing to disclose an issue this significant to prospective tenants is unacceptable.

To make matters worse, the unit has inadequate window coverings that let in significant light at night, air conditioning that doesn't work, and a smoke detector that doesn't function. We've raised all of these issues, and very little has been done to resolve them.

The company also doesn't publish rental prices, which makes it hard for newcomers to the area to know whether they're being offered a fair rate.

They also manage a newer building, Keval, which I'd personally avoid as well. Prices there are high, but our experience with their service and management does not justify paying luxury prices for such poor service.

If you're looking for a higher-end rental, I'd recommend The Maple or Curve instead. In my experience, they're a much better reflection of what comfortable, well-managed luxury living should actually look like.

one_star_reviews.text:
I would give Millennium Insurance 0 stars if I could.

I bought a new vehicle 12 days ago. Since it was a weekend and Millennium Insurance was closed, I used their online service to add the vehicle to my existing policy.

On Monday, when they opened, I went to their office in person hoping to speed things up. The front desk representative was extremely rude and did not even want to look into my situation. I was simply told that someone would contact me.

I waited until Friday. Nobody contacted me. I then called and spent 30 minutes on hold, only to be told that someone would contact me within 7 business days from the date of my online request.

Fine. I waited the full 7 business days — 10 actual days — and still nobody contacted me.

At that point, I found an old email from the person who had previously arranged my insurance policy and contacted him directly. He initially said he would help and asked me to answer some questions and provide documents. I did exactly that — including answering the same questions I had already submitted through the online application — and sent all the requested documents.

The next day, he replied saying that he could not help me and that I needed to call the front desk.

So I called again. This time I waited 40 minutes on hold. I provided my policy number and tried to find out what was happening, but instead of actually helping me, the representative transferred me to an automated voicemail system.

Two weeks have now passed, and I still cannot get insurance for my new vehicle.

Because I cannot insure the vehicle, I cannot legally drive it or even move it myself. I have already spent $500 on a tow truck just to get the vehicle where it needs to go.

This is an absolutely unacceptable level of customer service. I did not have a 5 star experience as I ve read about in all the reviews . There were massive communication breakdowns repeatedly throughout the 4 years .  I found out my lawyer went off on Materinty leave when I recieved a letter in the mail with the date for my discovery and a different Lawyers name was on it. He was useless and failed to follow up with afterwards even though I requested it twice, he also left me with the wrong infomartation that I was to then collect my reports from practicioners which sent me on a 6 month goose chase trying to collect stuff.
A copy of my income tax was sent to me via courier without any heads up it was coming,still not sire why they felt the need to send me a copy?? ,  the courier failed to notifiy me and just got into my apartment building and left it on a public table accessible to anyone .
I had 4 or 5 different legal aids , Zhabaz Kahn was the only one who seemed completly compentent. The other aid couldnt even reply to all questions I asked in emails, they could only answer one so I was repeatedly seeking follow ups.
At one point I told my Lawyer I wanted to be put on Payroll or Compensated for the amount of effort I ve been putting into this. That got me a meeting with her and a senior lawyer. I asked for a trauma senitive informed one and with in seconds of our meeting she asked me if I was a micro manager .. once I explained many of the reasons I was upset she offered that my lawyer could explain this to the owner and perhaps my expert Dr. Fees interest rates would be waived . This did happen, so thank you yo whomever made that decision . However, I did learn that my lawyer lied about the reason for the first Dr. Fees approval request , and in a conversation  I called her out and explained what accountability looks like and she was not as " pleasant " for the rest of the phone call.
I was not handling this well as I had many appointments, mental clarity , brain fog issues etc going on and I do not feel like my lawyer even tried to support or make things clearer for me until I had melt downs talking with her. Even though her profile blurb claims shes Empathetic to clients needs .
Towards the end of my case it was finally explained to me how SHE handles her cases and how my pracitioners just got added to a computer generated program . Even though I promptly and repeatedly updated any new practicioner I went to and told them who to remove ... I dont think there was one disbursement fee bill that came to me that was accurate due to their lack of updating my file.

My lawyer wasnt tracking any of the updates and reccommeded I go ahead with the expert Doctors appointment even though said Dr. reached out admitting she didnt see any ways she could help build my case and was willing to stop there and just charge us for the hours she had put into it. We ended up not using the report which cost me around $10,000 . I believe if my lawyer had been even looking at my pracitioners updates she would have understood what this Doctor was seeing and saying.
The only positive expressions of emotion that seemed real was when I settled and maybe a few happy face emojis from the last legal aide who supported the case.
As someone who has never dealt with a lawyer for any reason this was a terrible experience under a very stressful time in my life. I have a younger family member and friend whom are both lawyers that I repeatedly reached out to to help clarify plenty of things. I simply hope I never have to deal with one again, getting through this case has shown me that self representation might be worth the effort !

If your a senstive person or have any overwhelm thats causing you confusion or are expecting compassion and empathy , I highly recommend finding another law firm . This experience felt cold and induced so much unneccessary anxiety and stress.  I m glad this is over and I can move on

A Very Disappointing Experience at Shoppers Drug Mart

Today, August 20, at approximately 5:30 p.m., my partner visited this location after already having a frustrating experience at another branch of the same chain on Wilson Street in Ancaster.

The request was simple: a government-required photograph for a passport application.

My partner approached an employee who was stocking products in one of the aisles and asked where the passport photos were taken. The employee, a young woman, responded dismissively: “Go to the entrance, girl.”

“Girl”? I don't blame her for not knowing the answer, but I do question the lack of courtesy and respect in addressing a customer with such familiarity—especially someone who could easily be her mother. Whatever happened to basic customer service and respect, Shoppers Drug Mart?

What makes this even more disappointing is that only about 15 minutes earlier, my partner had requested the same service at the Wilson Street location. There, a young employee told her that he was actually planning to resign that afternoon and warned her that there was a good chance the passport photo would be rejected—and that he would not take responsibility for it.

What happened to Shoppers Drug Mart?

I wish your employees well, and I sincerely hope things improve for everyone working there. But after these experiences, we have no interest in using your services again.

What a shame. You have lost two customers over something as simple as basic courtesy, professionalism, and customer service.

I went here on a Thanksgiving afternoon when the banks were closed and tried to make a deposit. And I couldn't! They only accepted withdrawals, came here for nothing, now I am forced to wait until the branches open

I had a very disappointing experience at Ultramar Pipeline in Belleville.

I am a pipeline customer and came in to use the proper customer shower. The staff member, Virat, was working the night shift and told me to use the other washroom instead. That washroom is a public washroom, while the proper showers are separate facilities for customers.

When I asked to use the proper shower, I was told that the showers were being cleaned and that it would take about 30 minutes. I agreed to wait. I ended up waiting around 45 minutes, while the shower still wasn’t cleaned.

What makes this even worse is that Virat was still there in the morning, and the exact same situation was happening. The showers apparently still weren’t available, and I was again told to use the public washroom instead.

I don’t understand how a pipeline customer can be expected to use a public washroom when there are proper customer showers available. If the showers genuinely needed cleaning, they should have been properly cleaned and made available within a reasonable amount of time.

The biggest issue was the attitude and the way Virat dealt with me. Instead of trying to help a customer, he repeatedly insisted that I use the other washroom and gave me the same excuse from night until morning.

This was not just poor service — it was extremely disrespectful customer service.

Management should seriously look into this situation and speak with Virat about how customers are being treated. Customers should not have to argue with staff just to access the facilities they are supposed to be able to use.

Very disappointing experience. I will definitely think twice before stopping here again.

one_star_reviews.text:
Disappointing Landscaping Service

Unfortunately, our experience with West Coast Lawn & Gardens was disappointing, and our Strata ultimately made the decision to terminate their services and change contractors.

Since joining our Strata Council in the summer of 2025, I personally observed a consistent decline in the overall standard of landscaping maintenance at our property. The contractor significantly underquoted the property, and the quality and consistency of the work never met the expectations we had for our community.

West Coast Lawn & Gardens advised us that one of the main reasons for the declining standard was the time constraint of only three man-hours per week. While the limited hours may have been a contributing factor, we also felt that the available time was not being effectively planned or prioritized.

During regular property patrols, we repeatedly observed:

Significant weed growth throughout the plant beds.
Weeds becoming established and spreading due to a lack of timely control.
Landscape beds becoming increasingly neglected in appearance.
Too much emphasis on routine mowing and basic tasks, with insufficient attention to proactive weed management.
Rooftop plant beds being neglected unless we specifically requested that they be addressed.

The photographs I took on July 2, 2026 & July 16, 2025 clearly demonstrate some of the conditions we were dealing with.

We understand that maintaining a large strata property is challenging, and we appreciate that there can be legitimate time and resource constraints. However, residents and owners expect their landscaping contractor to properly assess the property, provide an appropriate level of service, and maintain the grounds to a reasonable and consistent standard.

After approximately a year of unsatisfactory service, our Council determined that it was time for a change. West Coast Lawn & Gardens was terminated as our landscaping contractor, and we have since moved forward with a new company.

This review reflects my personal experience and observations as a Strata Council member. We sincerely hope our new landscaping contractor can bring the level of care, attention to detail, and consistency that our property requires.

THINK TWICE BEFORE RENTING HERE

My experience living at Compten Management’s Holly Street property was absolutely terrible. If I could give zero stars, I would.

I strongly recommend that anyone looking for a place to live seriously consider other options before renting from this management company. My experience left me extremely frustrated and disappointed with how residents and their concerns are handled.

The communication and response from property management were extremely poor. When problems were brought forward, I often felt ignored, dismissed, or left to deal with issues myself. The superintendent was also extremely difficult to deal with when concerns needed to be addressed.

I also had serious concerns about security and my overall sense of safety in the building. I did not feel that my concerns were taken seriously or handled in a way that made me feel supported as a resident.

Maintenance was another major problem. In my experience, getting repairs addressed could take an unreasonable amount of time. I had an issue that took approximately THREE MONTHS to be resolved. That is completely unacceptable when you are paying rent and expecting basic maintenance to be handled in a reasonable timeframe.

What was even more frustrating was dealing with the various policies, fees, and charges. From my experience, it often felt like there was always another reason to charge residents money, while basic concerns and services were not being handled with the same urgency.

Overall, I found the experience stressful, frustrating, and extremely disappointing. I did not feel valued as a resident, and I did not feel that my concerns about safety, maintenance, or the living environment were properly addressed.

If you are considering renting here, DO YOUR RESEARCH FIRST. Read the reviews, ask questions, understand every fee and policy in your lease, and speak to current or former residents if you can.

Based on my personal experience, I would not choose to live here again.

They scheduled a viewing and upon arriving they just buzzed me in to see the unit myself without anyone from their team there.  They clearly don't care at all about security.  And I was in horror upon opening the unit that I was there to view - it was disgustingly dirty, dead bug carcasses everywhere, and I walked out immediately before any nasty bugs decided to take a trip with me back to my home.

This place looks like it's run by a corporate slump lord.  But the prices don't match.

FINAL UPDATE – Sept 9:
I have finally received the refund.

UPDATE – Sept 8:
Unfortunately, this issue is still not over. After weeks of follow-ups, KEY finally agreed to reduce the invoice to an agreement amount and refund to my credit card.

However, the refund has still not gone through. I now have to contact them yet again to have the refund reprocessed.

UPDATE – August 28:

This response is extremely disappointing and makes this situation even more frustrating.

I already contacted your Vice President, Cory Leurer, on August 20, and he responded to me directly. He specifically stated that my dispute would be answered “over the next 3 to 5 business days” with the intention of reaching a reasonable resolution.

Today is August 28, and I still have not received the promised response or resolution.

Yet your company is now publicly replying to my Google review asking me to contact Cory — the very person I already contacted and have been waiting for.

We are a small local restaurant. Our request is very simple: review a disputed $637 invoice, provide a proper explanation, and honour the timeline your own Vice President committed to.

Your Customer Service Manager has also already confirmed in writing, after reviewing your own call recording, that there was no conversation about service rates when the appointment was arranged.

I genuinely do not understand why such a straightforward dispute requires this much chasing and this much time.

If a company gives its customer a clear commitment of 3–5 business days, that commitment should be honoured.

I am still waiting for KEY Equipment Services to provide the response and reasonable resolution that was promised.
——————

Small business owners, please be very careful before calling KEY Equipment Services.

We are a small local restaurant and received an invoice of over $600 for a service visit of approximately 15 minutes.

What shocked me was not only the total amount, but the various charges added to the invoice, including service-related and administrative charges. Most importantly, none of these rates or charges were disclosed to us when we booked the service call.

I disputed the invoice and KEY’s own Customer Service Manager, Jennifer Craven, subsequently reviewed their call recording and confirmed in writing that there was no conversation about rates.

Their explanation was that because our business was already in their system and there was a KEY tag on our equipment, they assumed we were aware of their rates.

I find this extremely unreasonable. Being an existing customer does not mean a business should be assumed to know or automatically agree to current rates, minimum charges, administrative fees or other charges that were never disclosed when the service was authorized.

The technician was at our location for only approximately 15 minutes, yet we ended up with an invoice exceeding $600. As a small business, this is a substantial and unexpected expense.

Even more frustrating is what happened after we disputed it. We have followed up repeatedly and were eventually told the invoice was being reviewed by technical management to determine whether the charges were valid or whether a credit should be issued. We are still waiting, with no resolution and no clear timeline.

How long should a small business have to keep chasing a company just to have a disputed invoice properly reviewed?

I am sharing this experience to warn other business owners: before booking KEY Equipment Services, ask them to provide ALL rates, minimum charges, administrative fees, travel charges and any other possible fees IN WRITING before you authorize the service.

Our experience has been extremely disappointing. I will update this review if and when KEY provides a fair resolution.

I am writing to express my disappointment with the service I received regarding my CPAP machine pickup appointment.

I called your office to advise that I would be approximately 20 minutes late for my scheduled 3:15 p.m. appointment. This was simply a pickup of a replacement CPAP machine the same model I have always used. No special fitting, instruction, or consultation was required as I have used the same machine for years. Given that your office closes at 4:00 p.m., I was confident there would still be sufficient time to complete this straightforward transaction.

Unfortunately, when I called, I was directed to a national answering service rather than your local office. The answering service contacted your office and advised me that I would have to reschedule. They were unable to provide any assistance beyond that. What concerned me most was the dismissive attitude I encountered. The response I received amounted to, “Okay, no problem, we’ll cancel everything then,” which I found both unprofessional and disappointing.

This purchase represents approximately $2,500, not including future equipment replacements, supplies, and ongoing purchases that are part of being a CPAP customer. The experience has left me questioning whether I wish to continue doing business with an organization that appears to place so little value on customer service and reasonable accommodation.

I would also point out that closing at 4:00 p.m. can make it difficult for working individuals to attend appointments without significant scheduling challenges. While I understand businesses set their own hours, limited accessibility combined with a lack of flexibility for a minor delay creates a poor customer experience under this corporate mentality.

Based on this interaction, I no longer feel confident dealing with your office. I hope you will take this feedback seriously and consider whether this level of service reflects the experience you intend your customers to have.

They were supposed to mill a tree to make a harvest table for an Indigenous non-profit and have stopped responding to calls, emails and letters and will not return the wood. We had a terrible experience. Bad communication. He quoted work done in 3 weeks and it took over 3 months. We never knew when they would show up. The work done was less than desirable. It was bas craftsmanship.

Extremely disappointing and concerning experience with CustomWorx.

Our Indigenous non-profit organization entrusted CustomWorx with culturally significant and sacred artifact that is the property of our organization. Despite repeated attempts to resolve the matter, including numerous phone calls, emails, and registered letter, we have received little to no meaningful response regarding the return of our property.

We have serious concerns about how our property has been handled and believe the circumstances surrounding the possession and non-return of these sacred artifacts require accountability.

Communication has been extremely poor, with repeated unanswered calls, emails, texts, and registered correspondence. We have also raised concerns about representations made by the business, including images that appear to have been taken from other businesses and presented as examples of CustomWorx's own work.

This situation has been particularly upsetting because these are not simply ordinary items. They are culturally significant and sacred artifacts belonging to an Indigenous non-profit organization in Toronto.

We are documenting all communications and taking the appropriate legal steps to address the matter. We strongly encourage anyone considering doing business with CustomWorx to conduct their own due diligence and carefully document any property entrusted to the business.

This review is not about the recreation centre as a whole, but specifically about my experience with one swimming instructor. Unfortunately, there does not seem to be a separate rating/review system for instructors, so I am sharing my experience here.

My child is enrolled in Little Splash 1, and our instructor, Judy, has been a major disappointment.

The session is only 30 minutes, but on most days the instructor arrives around 3–4 minutes late, even when the parents and children are already waiting. The session also often ends only a few minutes later, and additional time is spent very slowly getting the children into their life jackets. As a result, the actual teaching time feels closer to 20 minutes.

Throughout the lesson, I frequently notice the instructor looking at the lesson sheet and the clock. The overall impression is that the focus is more on getting through the session than actively teaching the children.

For young children, especially 3–4-year-olds, swimming instruction should be energetic, engaging, clear and encouraging. Unfortunately, the instructions are often spoken so quietly and slowly that it is difficult for the children to hear. Communication also feels unnecessarily slow and hesitant.

The activities themselves are very basic, such as blowing bubbles or jumping into the water. What concerns me most is the lack of individual attention. For example, my child would sometimes not even put their face in the water when asked to blow bubbles, yet the instructor would not correct, encourage or guide them. Simply telling young children what to do without checking whether they are actually doing it is not effective teaching.

I have watched the other instructors during the same time slot, and the difference is very noticeable. The other instructors are energetic, communicate clearly, encourage the children and make the lessons fun. The children seem genuinely excited to participate with them. Unfortunately, our experience has been very different.

I strongly feel that the centre should have a proper feedback or rating system for individual instructors, because the quality of instruction can make a huge difference, especially for young children who are just learning to swim.

I hope the supervisor/manager takes this feedback seriously and evaluates the quality of instruction being provided. We would really appreciate having a different instructor for future sessions.

If you are enrolling your child in this program, I would recommend checking who the instructor .cancel it if you get JUDY .

Disappointing experience at the Cambridge location

I visited the Cambridge Mister Safety Shoes location on August 16, 2026, to use an employee safety-shoe voucher issued by my employer on August 13. The voucher clearly states: “Voucher expires 3 days from issue date.”

When I presented the voucher, the employee immediately told me that it was already expired. I explained that August 16 was the third day after the issue date, but she called the manager to confirm.

The employee (Sackary) then told me that they were counting August 13, 14 and 15 as the three days, meaning the voucher was considered expired on August 16. I was also told that there was no problem because my employer could simply issue another voucher and I could come back.

What disappointed me most was not simply the disagreement over the expiration date, but the way the situation was handled. The wording on the voucher is clearly open to interpretation, and instead of taking the time to clarify the policy professionally, I felt that my concern was dismissed.

Later that same day, I went to another Mister Safety Shoes location in Kitchener, and the exact same voucher was accepted on August 16 without any issue.

This is particularly concerning because it suggests that the expiration policy is either being interpreted differently between locations or that the Cambridge location applied the policy incorrectly.

I hope management reviews this situation and provides clear guidance to all locations so customers receive consistent information and are treated with the same level of professionalism regardless of which store they visit.

We are very disappointed in this archbishop and this Mass.

You wonder why churches and cathedrals are emptying out! There you have it! It starts at the top of the pyramid...

one_star_reviews.text: I contacted my local dealership regarding an uncompleted safety recall on my vehicle. While the official online Infiniti Owner Portal explicitly shows an "Active Open Recall" for my VIN, the service department claimed their internal warranty system does not display it due to the age of the campaign.The service department originally booked my appointment. However, an employee named Olivia Kirk called me back to state they could not find the recall for my VIN—despite it being clearly visible on infiniti.ca. After some pushback, her story changed from "cannot find the recall" to "the recall has already been completed," which is completely false. My portal history clearly displays exactly what work has been completed and what remains outstanding.When I reached out to corporate, they were equally unhelpful. They dismissed the online status by claiming the notification on their own official website has simply been a "mistake" since 2019.Frustrated by the runaround, I contacted Transport Canada. They ran my VIN and definitively confirmed an open recall for Recall ID: R151 (NHTSA Campaign Number: 10V074000). This recall was officially launched in February 2010 to fix a faulty fuel sender card inside the gas tank, which causes fuel gauges to inaccurately read 1/4 full when the tank is actually empty. This is a severe safety hazard that can cause the vehicle to stall unexpectedly on the highway.Transport Canada and other consumer safety agencies are now actively investigating this matter. If you are experiencing the same issue with your vehicle or dealership, I highly recommend reporting it directly through the Transport Canada online web form. Terrible customer service and a deeply disappointing experience.

UPDATE — AUGUST 2026:

Since posting my original review, Visa has refunded $9,000 of the approximately $14,000 I paid to this firm following my dispute concerning work I paid for but maintain I did not receive.

I also filed a complaint with the Law Society of Ontario. I am not disclosing the Law Society’s communications, conclusions or the outcome of my complaint. Separately, the Law Society’s publicly available website explains that it does not set legal fees and cannot reduce a lawyer’s bill. It also cannot award a client damages for alleged professional negligence. My dispute through Visa was a separate process.

I retained this firm in September 2025 and paid every retainer requested, totalling approximately $14,000. Despite repeatedly asking the firm to represent me in my court proceeding, I was ultimately informed that it would not represent me, would only prepare documents, and that I would be required to represent myself.

Even if the firm’s position is that it was retained only to prepare documents for me, that does not explain my experience nor explain the approximately $14,000 of fees I was billed. My file was not substantively reviewed until approximately February 2026, about five months after I retained the firm. During that period, the only written information I received was that my file was being reviewed, that the firm was working on other urgent matters, and that it intended to prepare a motion to change.

I never received a completed motion to change or any other completed court documents prepared by the firm. I was left without representation and without the completed work I understood I was paying for.

The firm’s response to my review describes our retainer arrangement and the work performed very differently from my experience. My concerns remain straightforward:
• I paid approximately $14,000 to the firm over a six-month period.
• I repeatedly requested representation and action on my file, remained up to date on every requested retainer, and repeatedly provided the documents needed to prepare the motion.
• Approximately five months after retaining the firm, I received an email informing me that it would not represent me at my court proceedings.
• I never received a completed motion or other completed court documents that I could use to represent myself.

The firm’s response also states that I am “known for writing negative reviews.” That characterization is not accurate. At the time of this update, this is only one of two negative reviews I have ever posted. I have written many positive reviews from this Google account as well as my older Google account as Darcy Neil. Readers can click my Google profile beside this review to view my public review history and assess that statement for themselves.

The $9,000 Visa refund is an important update. I am posting this information so readers have a complete and current account of my experience.

Except it took another 10 minutes just to pack the bag at 5:00 PM

And then the real surprise begins…

No utensils
No condiments
2 of the 4 sides were missing

At this point, I can only laugh.
Thank you, Swiss Chalet Canada! You guys really nailed the whole “order ahead for convenience” concept. 😂

Extremely disappointing experience. I purchased a warranty expecting peace of mind, but when I actually needed service, the experience became incredibly frustrating. My wheels were damaged during their service, and after two unsuccessful attempts to repair the issue, I was instructed by their own manager to take my vehicle elsewhere, get an estimate, and send it to them for reimbursement.

I followed their instructions and provided an estimate of approximately $1,100. After long delays and repeated follow-ups, they offered only $400 and later tried to describe that amount as my remaining warranty balance which is completely separate from the damage caused to my vehicle while it was in their care.

Communication has been extremely slow, responses take far too long, and even after sending a formal email requesting management-level resolution, I have received no response. The entire experience has left me feeling misled and taken advantage of. In my opinion, the way this situation has been handled is extremely unfair and unacceptable.

A warranty is only valuable if a company stands behind it when problems actually occur. Unfortunately, based on my experience, I cannot say that this company has handled this situation professionally, fairly, or responsibly. I absolutely cannot recommend this company based on my experience and would strongly encourage potential customers to carefully consider their options before purchasing a warranty from them.

Cash payments come with a discount, but without a detailed invoice. I also observed what appeared to be a troubling practice with Ghost Bond glue: containers bearing this brand seemed to have their original label removed and replaced with another, then be resold at a much higher price. I find this very concerning and deceptive.

I also witnessed a way of treating certain employees that I found disrespectful, humiliating, and degrading.

Finally, when I mentioned the possibility of suing him, Cam told me that the judge would be lenient because of his age, that it could take up to four years, and that I wouldn't win. I found this response intimidating and completely inappropriate.

For me, trust, honesty, and respect are essential. After this experience, I'm done. I will never do business with this clinic again.

This is the worst clinic that I ever knew. What is the point of the chairs that the companion of the client cannot wait inside? So the chairs is only for display? The receptionist was very rude. Horrible clinic. 😡 …

Very disappointing experience with Dr. Regan. Everything was smooth and pleasant for the first several months of my wife’s pregnancy, and we had no complaints. Then, during the final month, Dr. Regan suddenly disappeared completely from the picture, and my wife was only seen by the nurse, with no explanation.

Thankfully, she wasn’t there for the delivery. Even more disappointing, she never checked in afterward or followed up with my wife. The lack of communication and follow-up at such an important time was extremely disappointing. I would not recommend her.

One of the most unprofessional experiences we’ve had with a medical clinic.

My wife is 32 weeks pregnant and was receiving ongoing care with Dr. Sklar. She was going to be approximately 10 minutes late for an appointment, so I did the responsible thing and called the clinic while I was on my way to let them know.

Instead of getting a straightforward answer, the receptionist put me on hold for approximately 10 minutes. By the time she came back on the phone, we were already in the clinic parking lot. We were then told that the doctor would not see my wife and that we would have to reschedule.

She offered to reschedule for Tuesday next week, I simply declined to reschedule and ended the call because I wasn’t sure if Tuesday would work with my schedule.

The real problem came afterward.

When we called the clinic again later to arrange another appointment, the receptionist told us that because I had supposedly been rude during the previous conversation, the doctor might no longer see my wife.

I tried to explain what had actually happened and that I had not been rude. She would not let me finish speaking and hung up on me.

Think about that for a moment: a pregnant patient at 34 weeks may potentially lose access to her OB because a receptionist decided that her husband was “rude” during a phone call — and when he tried to clarify the situation, the receptionist simply ended the conversation.

If the clinic has a strict policy about being 10 minutes late, that’s fine. We can accept that. What we cannot accept is the unprofessional and disrespectful way this was handled, particularly when the issue concerns ongoing obstetrical care.

Receptionists are often the first point of contact between patients and a medical practice. They should be helping patients navigate care, not creating additional conflict and then refusing to communicate.

We are now having to look into transferring my wife’s care to another clinic because we no longer feel comfortable dealing with this office.

Dr. Sklar may be an excellent physician, but unfortunately our experience with the front office has completely overshadowed our experience with the practice. Clinic management should seriously review how patients are being treated and how communication with patients is being handled.

This was not simply a bad customer-service experience. This involved a 34-week pregnant patient and potentially disrupted her ongoing obstetrical care. That is what makes this experience especially unacceptable.

BEWARE OF MISLEADING BRANDING: PF Custom Countertops no longer exists.

Do not be fooled by this Google listing or the old company vehicles still driven around Edmonton. PF Custom Countertops was acquired and permanently closed down by FLOFORM Countertops in 2024.

This listing is maintained solely to capture searches for a reputable local Alberta fabrication shop that is no longer operational. In reality, you are dealing entirely with FLOFORM, where local manufacturing has been largely replaced by out-of-province operations (Saskatchewan) and British Colombia administrative outsourcing, resulting in lengthy delays and severe communication breakdowns for Alberta customers.

If you are looking for true local Alberta craftsmanship and direct accountability, look elsewhere.

Thanks for the coffee invite, but no amount of PR spin changes what is happening behind the scenes. Inviting former staff for a showroom tour doesn’t undo the dismantling of a legacy Alberta shop, nor does it address the corporate consolidation, outsourced administrative pipelines, and misleading dual-branding. If FloForm is so proud of its own operations, it should stand on its own brand rather than quietly leveraging PF’s legacy to capture local goodwill. Local customers deserve transparency, not marketing deflections.

Extremely Disappointing Experience

I had a very frustrating experience at this UPS Store regarding passport/ID photos.

My wife and I initially had our photos taken there, but both sets of photos were later rejected by the government. We returned to the store and explained the situation. They agreed to take another photo, but the customer service representative kept the original receipt.

Unfortunately, the second set of photos was also rejected. When we went back again, the store refused to take another photo, despite advertising that the photos are "guaranteed" if they are rejected for any reason.

What makes this even more disappointing is that their policy does not clearly state any limit on the number of retakes. The wording simply indicates that the photos are guaranteed if rejected. Yet when we tried to use that guarantee, the store refused to honor it.

The issue was never about getting something for free. We simply wanted a government-compliant photo after 2 failed attempts. Instead, we were met with poor customer service, inconsistent application of their own policy, and no real effort to resolve the problem.

I would not recommend this location for official government photos. If your application depends on having compliant photos, you may want to consider another provider.

I would like to share my experience with this dental clinic. Unfortunately, it has been a very negative one.
The dentist repaired a chipped filling for me, but the problem kept happening repeatedly. Initially, he repaired a small chipped portion of the tooth. About two weeks later, the filling chipped again, so I returned to have it repaired. Later, the dentist removed an even larger portion of the tooth and placed a much larger filling, supposedly to make it more secure.

Unfortunately, about a month later, this filling chipped again.

In total, I had to have the same filling repaired approximately three or four times, and every time the same problem happened again. In my opinion, this clearly indicates that the work was not done properly or to an acceptable standard.

What is especially frustrating is that I was charged twice for this treatment. I paid out of pocket once, and the clinic also billed my insurance for the treatment. Considering that the filling repeatedly failed and had to be redone because of the quality of the original work, I expected the repairs to be covered under the clinic’s warranty rather than being charged again.

Unfortunately, I am very disappointed with both the treatment and the way this situation was handled. I cannot recommend either this dentist or this clinic. In my experience, the work was not performed to a high standard, and the result was not durable.

I hope the clinic takes this feedback seriously and reviews both the quality of its dental work and how it handles warranty coverage for patients.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’ve been going to this Pizza Hut location for years because it’s the closest one to me, but after repeatedly having poor experiences, I no longer feel comfortable supporting this location or Pizza Hut in general.

The biggest issue is the management. In my experience, there is very little accountability when something goes wrong, and customer concerns are not handled professionally. I’ve had numerous issues with incorrect orders, improperly cooked food, missing or inadequate toppings, and overall inconsistent quality. I’ve also had to complain about finding hair in my food on multiple occasions, which raises serious concerns about hygiene and food-handling practices at this location.

Unfortunately, I have also personally experienced what I believe was food poisoning twice after eating from this location. I obviously cannot say with certainty what caused it, but after having that happen twice, it has made me extremely uncomfortable ordering from here again.

What makes this even more frustrating is that these don't seem to be isolated problems. Looking through other reviews, I’ve noticed similar complaints about missing toppings and poor order quality. When customers call to address these issues, the response can be rude rather than focused on resolving the problem and taking responsibility.

At this point, I’ve had enough. Customers should be able to expect basic things like properly prepared food, reasonable hygiene, accurate orders, and respectful customer service.

For me, Domino’s has been a much better experience. I find the value and consistency better, and I don’t have to worry about whether my pizza will actually have the toppings or cheese I ordered. If you’re looking for better customer service, consistency, and value, I would personally recommend going elsewhere.
After years of being a customer, it’s disappointing to say this, but I will not be returning to this Pizza Hut location.

Extremely disappointing customer service at the Michael Kors store in Vaughan Mills today, September 5, 2026, at 5:30 PM.

There were three cashiers at the checkout, and the female cashier standing in the middle had long, straight black hair. Even while I was waiting in line, her attitude was noticeably impatient and unfriendly.

She brought out a packaged white bag from the back. I said I wanted to check it before taking it, and she told me I had to pay first and could then go to the end of the cashier area to check it. I followed her instructions and paid.

After checking the bag, I found a very obvious black mark near the bottom center. Since the bag was white, it was extremely noticeable. I asked to exchange it for another one.

She rolled her eyes and said she couldn’t possibly open every bag for customers to check. But I was NOT asking her to open every bag—I had already purchased the bag, followed her instructions, and found an obvious defect. I simply wanted an undamaged one.

I eventually asked if I could take another bag from outside, and she said yes. I took the replacement, which had no packaging, and she was not even willing to give me the plastic protective film that had been used to wrap the original bag.

What makes this experience particularly frustrating is that I have shopped from Zara, Uniqlo to Louis Vuitton, Gucci—and I have never been made to feel unreasonable for wanting to choose and check the item I am purchasing. How did this become a problem at Michael Kors?

While I was waiting, I also saw her joking and fooling around with a male coworker, and she was perfectly capable of smiling then. Yet when dealing with a customer, the attitude was completely different.

The issue isn’t whether she smiled at me. It’s the dismissive attitude, eye-rolling, refusal to reasonably address an obvious defect, and making a customer feel like a burden for simply wanting an undamaged product.

I strongly encourage the store manager to review what happened at 5:30 PM today and identify this employee. This experience was unacceptable and reflects very poorly on the store and the brand.
