⭐ 1 STAR — EXTREMELY DISAPPOINTING EXPERIENCE

I am absolutely appalled by how I was treated at this walk-in clinic.

I arrived at approximately 6:20 p.m., specifically after checking that the clinic was open until 7:00 p.m. I even called beforehand and was told they were open. I work full-time and could only come after work, and despite the bad weather and heavy rain, I drove there because I have been dealing with a very painful toothache and needed to see a doctor.

When I arrived, the door was already locked even though there were still approximately 40 minutes until the posted closing time. A woman came to the door and told me they were not taking any more patients because they had two patients left to see and were going home early because of the bad weather.

What upset me even more was her attitude. She was extremely dismissive and appeared to be smirking while I was explaining that I was in pain and had driven there specifically because their posted hours said they were open. I was literally crying and begging her to please just ask the doctor if they could see me, and she repeatedly told me, “No, we’re going home early.”

I explained that I work full-time and could not simply come back tomorrow. She showed absolutely no compassion or concern. I wasn't demanding that the doctor see me — I was asking her to at least speak to the doctor and explain the situation, especially considering I had arrived 40 minutes before closing.

What made the situation even more frustrating was that another person came up and she helped that person, while continuing to refuse to help me.

If a clinic is going to stop accepting patients before its posted closing time, that needs to be clearly communicated. Patients should not check the hours, call to confirm the clinic is open, drive through bad weather while in pain, and then arrive to find the doors locked well before closing.

I understand that staff want to get home safely in bad weather — so did I. But I also had to drive through that same weather to get there. I relied on the information I was given that the clinic was open until 7:00 p.m.

The complete lack of empathy and the way I was spoken to while I was visibly upset and in pain was unacceptable. I left without even being given the courtesy of having my situation brought to the doctor's attention.

After this experience, I would not recommend this clinic to anyone. Patients deserve to be treated with basic compassion and respect, especially when they are sick or in pain.

one_star_reviews.text:
This is the first time in my life that I have ever left a negative review for a restaurant, but unfortunately, this experience needs to reach the management and, hopefully, the corporate office at Boston Pizza.

Boston Pizza has always been one of my favourite restaurant chains. Whenever I travel to different cities, my family and I often choose Boston Pizza because we have always had good experiences. Unfortunately, this visit was a complete disappointment.

I called ahead of time to make a reservation on the patio because I was travelling with my dog. When I called, I specifically asked whether the patio was pet-friendly. I was initially told that it was not, but the employee said they would speak with the manager. I was later told by the manager that my dog could join us on the patio. There was also a sign at the restaurant clearly stating that the patio was pet-friendly.

Because I had called ahead and made a reservation, I expected the patio and our table to be ready when we arrived. Instead, the patio was not even ready to receive customers. They did not have the key to open it, and once it was opened, our table was dirty and covered in dust. It had clearly not been cleaned before our arrival.

The condition of the patio was honestly unacceptable. There were leaves, garbage, and pigeon feathers everywhere. It looked like the patio had not been cleaned or maintained for quite some time. Considering that I had specifically called ahead and made a reservation, I expected at least a clean table and a reasonably clean dining area.

What made the experience even worse was the attitude of our server. When she came to take our order, she stayed at the patio entrance and essentially yelled our questions and order from the doorway because she said she was afraid of my dog. My dog is a small, extremely friendly and well-trained dog. He did not move from his spot during the entire time we were there. He regularly travels with us and is trained to behave appropriately in restaurants, hotels, and even during air travel. He was completely calm and caused absolutely no disturbance.

Approximately 20 minutes after we arrived, a person who I believe was the manager finally came out and wiped down the table. However, the chairs were still dusty, and there was no apology or acknowledgment of the condition of the patio or the fact that we had been left waiting with a dirty table.

We decided to stay because we had made a reservation and there are not many options in this city for people travelling with pets. However, the service throughout the evening was extremely disappointing. Our server continued to take our order from the doorway rather than coming to the table, and communication was very difficult. Unfortunately, the level of service and professionalism was far below what I have come to expect from Boston Pizza.

For the first time in my life, I decided not to leave a tip. I do not normally do this, but the service we received was so poor that I felt it was justified on this occasion.

I am posting this review because I genuinely hope it reaches management and the Boston Pizza corporate office. I will also be including photos showing the condition of the patio when we arrived.

Boston Pizza is a well-known Canadian restaurant brand, and I sincerely hope the company takes situations like this seriously. There should be consistent standards for cleanliness, customer service, staff training, and patio maintenance across all locations in Canada.

I am not writing this review because I dislike Boston Pizza. Quite the opposite — I am writing it because it has always been one of my favourite restaurants, which is why this experience was so disappointing.

I hope management takes this as an opportunity to create an action plan, improve the cleanliness and maintenance of this location, properly train the staff, and ensure that customers receive the level of service that the Boston Pizza brand is supposed to represent.

I had a very disappointing consultation with Aman Singh at MEWI Immigration Services. I booked the consultation expecting professional and respectful guidance about our PR options, but the way I was spoken to was rude, dismissive, and insulting.

When I explained that finding another employer willing to support a closed work permit is extremely difficult, I was told that I was “not trying properly,” that “the problem is with you,” and that if I could not find another job, I should “pack my bags and go home.”

I also asked about possible study options for my husband, but the response was dismissive and made me feel that our situation was being judged rather than properly explained. I was also told that age was a major issue and that we could soon be too late for other options.

I completely understand that immigration consultants sometimes have to give difficult or negative advice. My issue is not that I did not hear what I wanted to hear. My issue is the disrespectful and humiliating way the advice was communicated.

People pay for consultations because immigration decisions are already stressful and complicated. They deserve honest, clear, and professional advice—not to be blamed, belittled, or told to “pack your bags and go home.”

I left the consultation feeling insulted and discouraged rather than properly informed about our options. Based on my experience, I would not recommend this consultation service.

His behaviour felt extremely unprofessional and unnecessarily hostile. Instead of giving objective advice, he seemed to direct his frustration toward the clients seeking his help.

I am writing this review to urge Belairdirect to do better when handling simple customer inquiries.
​A few years ago, I called customer service to ask a hypothetical question regarding potential damage from a pothole. No claim was ever opened, no financial payout occurred ($0 paid out), and no collision took place. However, I recently discovered that Belairdirect logged this simple phone inquiry into the provincial AutoPlus database as a "100% At-Fault Collision Claim."
​While my official AutoPlus report confirms $0 paid out and 7 years of claims-free driving history, logging a basic inquiry as an at-fault collision misrepresents my driving record to other insurers and creates unnecessary hurdles for consumers.
​When customers call with innocent questions, customer representatives must be transparent and ensure non-claim events are categorized accurately. I have formally submitted a correction request with my documentation to their customer experience team and expect this inaccuracy in the MTO/AutoPlus database to be rectified promptly.

one_star_reviews.text:
I had a very concerning customer-service experience at Future Tech on Thursday, August 20 around 3 p.m.

I went in for a Samsung screen replacement and first asked whether they used an original Samsung screen. The employee told me they did not, but offered an aftermarket screen for about $240.

Since I would be paying $240 to have a non-original part installed in my personal phone, I asked for the name of the screen manufacturer so I could research its quality, reliability, and reviews before agreeing to the repair.

The employee seemed very reluctant to tell me the brand, although he eventually said the name once. When I asked him to repeat it because I had forgotten it, he responded:

“I said it once. I’m not gonna say it again.”

I explained that I work in IT and simply wanted to know what product was going into my phone before paying for the repair. After I asked again, he told me:

“I won’t give you service. Go straight to Samsung.”

I find this completely unacceptable. Asking for the manufacturer of an aftermarket part before paying $240 to have it installed is a very reasonable customer question.

The refusal to provide basic information about the product, followed by refusing me service because I continued asking about it, made me seriously question the transparency and professionalism of this business.

Customers should be able to know what parts are being installed in their devices before agreeing to a repair.

one_star_reviews.text:
If I could leave negative stars I would!

I am absolutely appalled by the way my 11-month-old son and I were treated at the Citadel Village Shoppers Drug Mart tonight.

My son has croup. We went to Sturgeon Hospital, where we were told the wait to receive the steroid medication he needed could be approximately eight hours, as his oxygen levels were stable. The triage nurse suggested that I try the prescribing pharmacist at Shoppers Drug Mart to see if they could prepare the medication.

At approximately 11:40 p.m., I walked over with my sick 11-month-old and explained the situation to the prescribing pharmacist. I was refused because, according to the pharmacist, they were “closing.” I stood there completely dumbfounded. There were still 20 minutes before midnight.

I was told that it would be a lengthy process and that the pharmacist did not feel comfortable doing it because it would be rushed.

I understand that pharmacists have procedures and professional responsibilities and I would never expect anyone to compromise patient safety. But what happened next made this experience even more upsetting.

I called another Shoppers Drug Mart location on the south side of St. Albert and explained the exact same situation. Their prescribing pharmacist told me that if I could get there before the front doors were locked at midnight, he would stay past closing to fulfill the request. He explained that he simply didn't have keys to let me in after the doors were locked.

That pharmacist showed compassion, understanding and a willingness to help a desperate mother with a sick infant. That is what patient care looks like. And the best part is, it took him less than 20 minutes to do this for us.

The contrast between the two experiences was shocking.

One pharmacist found a way to help a sick child and went above and beyond to make sure we got the medication we needed. The pharmacist at the Citadel Village location refused to help while there was still time before closing, leaving me to scramble to another location with my sick baby.

I am not asking pharmacists to break rules or put patient safety at risk. I am asking for compassion, professionalism and a willingness to help when a sick infant and a desperate parent are standing in front of you.

To the pharmacist who stayed late to help us: thank you. Your kindness meant more to me tonight than you probably realize.

To the Citadel Village location: do better. A sick 11-month-old deserved better than being turned away while there was still an opportunity to help.

I sincerely hope management reviews what happened and considers how this situation could have been handled with more compassion and patient-focused care.

My first visit with the cardiologist was a great experience. The doctor was kind, professional, and I felt very comfortable with the care we received. I had a great female ultrasound tech. I was able to breastfeed while she did the ultrasound. The other people that worked there taking height and weight were also great to deal with.

Unfortunately, the second visit was an entirely different experience. The ultrasound technician was extremely rude, impatient, and made an already stressful situation with my 6-month-old much worse.

My baby was moving and crying during the ultrasound, and the technician repeatedly instructed me to hold him down by his arms and legs. This only made my son more upset. He also kept telling me to talk to my baby, which I was already doing, but I could clearly see that my son was extremely uncomfortable and distressed. At that point, I did not feel that forcibly holding him down was going to help the situation.

I asked the technician if what we were doing was actually working, and his response was, “What do you think?” I found this incredibly rude and completely inappropriate, especially in a pediatric setting.

He continued becoming increasingly frustrated, gave instructions that were difficult for me to understand, and at one point threw his hands up and said, “We’re done.” By the end of the appointment, I was sweating, extremely anxious, and left shaking with anger over how we had been treated.

I understand that ultrasounds on babies can be difficult and that they don't always cooperate. I also understand that the technician needs to do his job. However, there is a huge difference between managing a difficult appointment and making a parent feel intimidated, frustrated, and unsupported.

The cardiologist himself has been wonderful, and I have no complaints about the doctor. My concern is entirely with the ultrasound technician. Based on this experience, I would absolutely refuse to have this technician care for my child again.

Parents bringing their children in for medical care should be treated with patience, respect, and compassion. This experience fell very far short of that.

Unfortunately, a very disappointing experience.

We contacted Valérie Flat for guidance and advice with our immigration process to Canada. Given our situation, she specifically recommended the SWAP/Young Professionals program.

My main regret concerns the support and information we received regarding our status in Canada and the deadlines for completing the necessary steps. At the time, we were both employed in Canada, my husband working for Hydro-Québec, and the consequences of this situation were significant for our family.
In hindsight, I would have expected a much more rigorous approach from an immigration professional regarding deadlines, the procedures to follow with IRCC, and the potential impact on our right to work and remain in Canada.

This experience profoundly affected our plans for a life in Canada, and we ultimately had to leave the country. Today I am sharing our experience so that future clients will remember to ask in writing and very precisely what steps need to be taken before their status expires and what the risks are in case of exceeding the deadlines.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am absolutely appalled by the way my mother was treated at Barry Denture Clinic. My mother recently began the process of getting dentures due to health reasons. A few days after her initial appointment, she realized that an option normally offered to other patients had never been presented to her.
During her most recent visit, she simply asked the receptionist why this option had not been offered. The receptionist responded by telling her that it was “only provided to people who can afford it.”
I find this response completely disgraceful, disrespectful and unacceptable. Who is this receptionist to make assumptions about someone's financial situation? She has absolutely no knowledge of my family's finances or what my mother can and cannot afford. Every patient deserves to be informed of ALL available treatment options, regardless of their perceived financial situation. It is up to the patient, not the receptionist, to decide what is financially feasible for them.
Getting dentures is already a significant life change. It can be emotionally difficult, affect someone's confidence and self-image, and come with considerable financial stress. The last thing anyone going through this process needs is to be judged, embarrassed or belittled by someone who is supposed to be helping them.
What makes this situation even more upsetting is that these comments were made in front of a waiting room full of other patients. My mother went into this clinic expecting professionalism, compassion and respect. Instead, she was made to feel embarrassed and judged simply for asking about an option that should have been presented to her in the first place.
No patient should ever have to feel that their financial situation determines the level of respect they receive or the treatment options they are entitled to know about. This behaviour is completely unacceptable, especially in a healthcare setting where patients may already be feeling vulnerable.

I visited this location at approximately 11:30 PM on Tuesday, September 1. I ordered the Pick-Up Special online, which is advertised as “Medium Pepperoni (or any regular topping) for only $11.99” and is shown with a pepperoni pizza.

After placing my order and paying, I received a plain cheese pizza. When ordering, selecting pepperoni showed an additional $2.50 charge, which made it seem like the $11.99 special already included pepperoni and the extra charge was for additional pepperoni. Based on the wording and picture, I reasonably expected the advertised pepperoni pizza.

When I noticed the issue, I calmly explained the confusion to the two employees working and asked if they could add pepperoni or provide some type of resolution. Instead, I was told there was nothing they could do. One employee abruptly told me to contact customer support, while the other agreed there was an issue but shifted the blame to the company. Neither employee made any real attempt to resolve a very simple problem.

Mistakes and misunderstandings happen, but the way this was handled was disappointing. Remaking a basic pepperoni pizza or offering another reasonable solution would have easily resolved the situation.

There are 2 things I believe need improvement:

1. The website: Clearly explain whether the $11.99 special includes pepperoni/one regular topping and why pepperoni appears as an additional $2.50 charge.

2. Customer service: Staff should listen to customer concerns respectfully and make an effort to find a solution instead of dismissing the issue or blaming the company.

I’ve never left a bad review before, even though the same thing happens almost every time I order at this location.
The servers repeatedly try to ignore what I’m actually asking for and ring in a “meal” instead of the order I specifically requested: individual pieces of chicken only. I always have to repeat myself several times before they finally bring up the menu with individual pieces of chicken (dark or white meat), which they apparently keep underneath the counter.

I know exactly what I want. Please don’t pretend not to understand my order just to push me into purchasing a meal I did not ask for. I understand that upselling is part of the job, but once a customer has clearly said no, that should be respected. Continuing to ignore the customer’s actual order is not upselling—it’s simply frustrating and disrespectful.

Tonight, a female server did the exact same thing again. I was too tired to keep repeating myself, so I told her directly that I wanted the menu for individual pieces of chicken—the one kept underneath the counter.

She still wouldn’t stop. She repeatedly pointed to the electronic menu behind me and insisted that “everything is listed there.” Several times.

When I clearly said, “I just want 6 pieces of dark meat chicken,” she kept asking, “So you want the 6-piece meal?” while simultaneously entering the meal into her register.

At that point, I honestly didn’t even know what else to say. I didn’t care about the price difference. I simply wanted to order what I wanted, in a portion I could actually finish, without having to argue or repeat myself every single time.

And it didn’t end there.

I ordered 3 wings and 3 thighs. When I got home and opened the box, I found 3 drumsticks and 3 thighs instead.

So not only was my order repeatedly misunderstood or ignored, but the final order was also incorrect.

Please listen to what your customers are actually ordering. If a customer says they do not want a meal, stop trying to force a meal onto their order. And if they specifically order wings, don’t substitute them with drumsticks without asking.

I chose to put those frustrations aside because of our longstanding relationship with the company. Unfortunately, combined with the difficulty getting callbacks and this most recent experience, it has become clear to me that the level of customer service simply isn't what it used to be or what I thought it was. There has been a noticeable shift over the years.

What made this even more disappointing is that I contacted Canuck as another option, feeling completely confused and frustrated on where to start all over. Even though they were also booking significantly ahead, they still made a big effort to accommodate my home and, more importantly, made me feel like my business mattered. That difference in customer service really stood out.

I don't normally leave negative reviews, but after more than 15 years as a customer, being told to simply go somewhere else was incredibly disappointing.

The reason I'm writing this review is that I came across the clinic's address by chance today and remembered my experience with them four years ago. I visited this clinic to get a full set of dentures. I booked my first appointment, and they examined my gums and confirmed they were healthy. I met the dentist, who was from Athens, Greece. He was very kind and polite. I continued with this for four or five visits, and I was very excited about my new teeth. However, I had an appointment to get the dentures, probably the last or second-to-last one, and it was canceled. I was so excited to get my teeth, so I asked my eldest daughter to help me and accompany me to translate. She was with me at all the sessions to translate between me and the dentist. I told her that my appointment, which I had been waiting for for over a month, had been canceled. My daughter said she would call the clinic, which she did. We called, but no one answered. So we went to the clinic, and it was closed, but there was an elderly blonde woman, about sixty-five years old, looking at us from the office.  We rang the bell twice, and after a few minutes, she opened the door and said, "Call us, we're outside!" (laughing). We saw her through the glass. My daughter said she would call to find out what was wrong. We called her and asked what the problem was. She said she would be at the door in a few minutes, and indeed, she came a little while later. She was carrying a small plastic bag, no more than 15 cm x 15 cm, containing her dentures. She opened the door barely wide enough for her palm and wrist, and my daughter asked, "What's this?" She replied, "These are for your son. He'll try them on at home, and if he has any problems, call the clinic." Of course, I was very annoyed, and my daughter asked, "Where's the dentist? One of our appointments was canceled, and another was ignored. We came to your clinic to find out what problems caused the dentist to cancel one appointment and ignore the other." After a few minutes of arguing, the woman came out, stood in the doorway, and said, "Here are your dentures. That's it."  She picked it up with the tip of her finger as if it were something disgusting or contagious. I grabbed the bag and threw it inside the clinic. Because of this rude treatment from the clinic and the woman, homeless people gathered around my daughter and my car and attacked us. They were standing in front of the clinic door. There were about four homeless people, and the woman inside the clinic was the cause of the incident; she didn't care. Unfortunately, I haven't received any response from the dentist, who is of Greek origin, whom I thought was a respectable doctor, and whom I had hoped would contact me, neither by phone nor by message. This is my experience with them. It's a terrible and disrespectful clinic. They should be boycotted, their medical licenses revoked, the clinic closed, and they should be banned from practicing dentistry throughout Canada. They should be held accountable under Canadian and international law for their disrespect for the dental profession, and all the employees of this clinic should be held accountable. Nowhere in the world have I heard of or seen a clinic hand out dentures on the sidewalk in the middle of the street, amidst dust, car exhaust, and obstructing the road.

Warranty concerns have often resulted in requests to “bring it back,” “try this,” or schedule another appointment. Each visit involves a 30-minute drive each way, and on several occasions, my truck has been kept for up to three days, only for the original issue to remain unresolved.

One GPS issue required my truck to return to the dealership five different times.

Most recently, after purchasing my F-450, I brought it in for a safety inspection. Rather than feeling that the main concerns were being addressed, I was told that the window tint needed to be removed and that the taillights were not factory equipment. This added to my impression that there is always another reason for an additional visit, creating more inconvenience and lost time.

I have given Peninsula Ford many opportunities, having brought three different Ford trucks there. Unfortunately, my experience has been consistent: routine maintenance and detailing have been satisfactory, but I have lost confidence in the dealership’s ability to diagnose and repair warranty, mechanical, or electrical issues efficiently.

Customers should not have to make multiple trips or leave a vehicle at the dealership for days only to receive it back with the same problem unresolved.

I am deeply concerned about the liturgical practices at this church and believe they warrant the attention of the archdiocese.

I attended a Sunday service that was presented as a Mass, despite no priest being present. Laypeople led the service, including the proclamation of the Gospel and what appeared to be a homily. During a portion described as spiritual Communion, attendees were invited to receive apples that had been placed on the altar at the beginning of the service.

Under Catholic canon law, a validly ordained priest is required for the celebration of the Eucharist. A lay-led service cannot validly celebrate Mass, and the homily at Mass is reserved to a priest or deacon.

I urge the archdiocese to investigate the circumstances, clarify whether this was an authorized Sunday celebration in the absence of a priest, and ensure that the faithful are clearly informed about the nature of the service and the Eucharist. It should be clear that the celebration is not a Mass and the manner in which these celebrations are being conducted would benefit from scrutiny.
